It is a webhook that receives a POST with JSON and responds with a generated Excel file to the waiting caller, which needs an internet-facing server outside Claude.

It is a daily scheduled job that reads workflows from the n8n REST API, compares them with files in GitHub, commits any changes, and posts Slack notifications, all of which a cloud scheduled task can do with HTTP API keys and the Slack connector.
It is a webhook with a Respond to Webhook node that returns a reply to a waiting HTTP caller, which needs an internet-facing server outside Claude.

This is a Telegram chatbot that other people message and that must reply promptly to each message, so it needs an always-on server to receive Telegram's webhook, which a scheduled task, skill, or artifact on a subscription can't do.
It is a webhook that waits for callers and responds with the generated audio binary (or a JSON error), so it needs an internet-facing server outside Claude to answer those synchronous requests.

The WhatsApp Trigger needs an always-on public callback URL for Meta to post incoming user messages to, which a Claude subscription can't provide, even though the Sheets polling and WhatsApp sending parts could run as scheduled tasks.

This is a Telegram chat bot that answers incoming messages from a user in real time via a Telegram webhook trigger, so it needs an always-on server to receive messages and reply, which a subscription scheduled task, skill, or artifact cannot provide.
It is a WhatsApp chatbot that answers messages from customers through a webhook-triggered, always-on endpoint, which needs hosting outside Claude.
This is a public WhatsApp chatbot that must receive incoming messages via a webhook from Meta and reply to users who message it, which needs an always-on internet-facing server outside Claude.

The chat-triggered agent is used by its owner to ask for a niche and get a YouTube trend summary, which works as a skill chatted with in Claude (or an artifact page) that calls the YouTube Data API with the owner's key, filters videos by duration, and has Claude summarize the results, so no public hosting is needed.
The workflow is triggered by a POST webhook that waits on a Respond to Webhook node to return the summary to the caller, so it needs an internet-facing server outside Claude.

This is a WhatsApp chat bot that receives Meta webhook calls from customers, including a GET verification endpoint that must return the hub.challenge, so it needs an always-on public server outside Claude.

The owner runs the Drive-to-Qdrant ingestion manually and chats with the documents themselves, so a skill can do both using the Google Drive connector, Claude models, and HTTP calls to Qdrant, OpenAI embeddings and Telegram with the owner's keys, and the chat step stands in for the delete approval.

This is a chat-based data analyst for the owner's own use that queries a Google Sheet and does calculations, so it can run as a skill the owner chats with in Claude using the Google Drive connector or the Sheets API, with no public server needed.

The form is the owner's own input, so a skill they chat with in Claude can take the topic, draft the posts, ask for approval in the conversation, then publish to X, LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram and send the results to Gmail and Telegram, using HTTP APIs and connectors with the owner's keys.

The owner chats with it to request posts, and every step (Google Docs/Drive/Gmail connectors, web search, image generation and imgbb over HTTP, X/Facebook/Instagram/LinkedIn publishing via their APIs with the owner's keys, and the approval step done in the chat itself) can run as a Claude skill, so no public server is needed.

The workflow only exists to expose Google Calendar and a few helper functions (case conversion, random user data, jokes) as MCP tools for an AI agent, which Claude does itself with its Google Calendar connector and its own abilities.

The workflow is a personal-assistant agent whose only job is to give an AI chat the Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Sheets tools (through an MCP server), and Claude does that itself with its own connectors.

The Telegram trigger is only the owner sending a TikTok link, so it can become a skill they chat with in Claude, and every other step (RapidAPI, Perplexity, captions.ai, JSON2Video and Blotato over HTTP with API keys, OpenAI transcription, Claude for the rewriting, Google Sheets connector) is an API call Claude can make.

This is a Telegram chat bot that other people message and that replies to each message as it arrives, so it needs an always-on server to receive Telegram webhooks, which a subscription scheduled task, skill, or artifact can't provide.

This is a chat agent with memory and a web search tool that the owner can chat with directly as a Claude skill (Claude has its own web search and conversation memory), and the n8n chat trigger is used only as the owner's own chat interface, not a public endpoint.

It is a manually triggered demo that chains OpenAI calls (chat, completions, DALL-E, Whisper transcription via HTTP) with no webhook or public endpoint, so it can run as a skill or artifact using Claude models and HTTP APIs with the owner's OpenAI key.

This is a simple chat-triggered LLM chain with a fixed polite-assistant prompt, which the owner can use as a skill chatting in Claude (Claude itself replaces the Hugging Face Mistral model), so no external hosting is needed.

This is a chat agent with web search (SerpAPI, Wikipedia) and memory that the owner uses themselves, so it can run as a skill they chat with in Claude, which has its own web search and models, and no public server is needed.

It is a manual-trigger batch job that calls HTTP APIs with an API key, scores companies with an AI model, and reads and writes a Google Sheet, so it can run as a Claude skill or scheduled task using the Google Sheets/Drive connector and Claude for scoring, with no server needed.

It is a daily schedule-triggered pipeline (Claude generates the idea and Veo3 prompt, HTTP calls to fal.ai Veo3 and Blotato with API keys, Google Sheets connector) with no inbound caller waiting on a reply, so it can run as a cloud scheduled task.

The workflow is a POST webhook whose callers wait for the reply and receive the generated .xlsx file in the response, so it needs a server on the internet to answer them.

This is a daily scheduled job that reads workflows from the n8n REST API with an API key, compares them with files in GitHub through its HTTP API, commits any changes and posts updates to Slack, all of which a Claude cloud scheduled task can do with HTTP calls and the Slack connector.
The workflow is a webhook API endpoint whose callers wait for a text reply from the Respond to Webhook node, so it needs a server on the internet to answer them, outside Claude.
It is a Telegram bot that other people message and that must reply in real time via a webhook trigger, so it needs an always-on server outside Claude to receive and answer those messages.
The workflow is a POST webhook API endpoint whose callers wait for the generated ElevenLabs audio to be returned as a binary response, so it needs a hosted server that answers requests.

The WhatsApp Trigger needs a public webhook that Meta calls with incoming customer messages and that must answer Meta's verification challenge, and the WhatsApp Cloud API offers no way to poll for those messages, so it needs hosting outside Claude even though the sheet-polling and reply-sending parts could run as scheduled tasks.
It is a WhatsApp chatbot that customers message, triggered by WhatsApp webhooks that require an always-on public endpoint to receive and reply in real time, so it needs hosting outside Claude.

This is a private assistant that only the owner uses (it has an allow-list of one chat ID), so it can become a Claude skill the owner chats with directly, using voice input in the Claude app, the Gmail and Google Calendar connectors, and the Baserow API with the owner's key, with no need for a hosted Telegram bot.

It is a public WhatsApp chatbot whose webhook trigger must receive messages from other people in real time and reply to each one, which needs an always-on internet-facing server rather than a scheduled task, skill or artifact.

This is a chat agent the owner talks to. It runs YouTube Data API searches, filters by video length, and summarizes trends, so it can become a Claude skill that calls the YouTube API with the owner's Google API key and analyzes the results in chat.

The workflow starts from a POST webhook and sends the summary back through Respond to Webhook, so it needs a public endpoint on a server that answers callers while they wait, which a Claude subscription cannot provide.

The workflow is a WhatsApp bot that customers message: Meta's webhook needs a public endpoint that answers the GET verification challenge and receives incoming messages in real time, so it needs hosting outside Claude even though the RAG answer itself could be done with Claude.

Both parts are owner-driven, so a Claude skill can run them: one lists and downloads files from the Google Drive connector, extracts metadata with Claude, and embeds and upserts or deletes Qdrant points through HTTP with the owner's OpenAI and Qdrant keys, asking for delete confirmation in chat instead of the Telegram approval; the other answers questions by querying Qdrant and appending the chat history to Google Docs (if Qdrant stays on localhost, it must run from the owner's own computer rather than the cloud).

This is a chat agent the owner uses to query a Google Sheet of transactions with filters and calculations, and the chat trigger isn't set to a public page, so it can become a Claude skill that reads the sheet through the Google Drive connector or the Sheets API and does the analysis itself.

The owner fills in the form, so this works as a Claude skill or artifact: Claude drafts the posts and does the SerpAPI research, the email approval becomes a confirmation in chat, and image generation, imgbb upload, Facebook/Instagram/X/LinkedIn posting and the Gmail/Telegram result notices all run through connectors or HTTP APIs with the owner's keys, with no outside caller waiting on a server.

The owner chats to request a post, and everything after that (reading prompt and schema docs from Google Docs, generating content and images, saving to Drive and imgbb, approving, and publishing to X, Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn through their APIs) can run as a Claude skill using connectors and HTTP calls with the owner's keys, with the Gmail approval step done in the chat instead.

The workflow mainly exposes MCP servers (Google Calendar tools plus trivial text-case, random-data and joke functions) for an AI agent. Claude covers this directly with its Google Calendar connector and its own abilities, and the n8n chat agent is just a demo client.

The workflow is an MCP server exposing Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Sheets tools to a chat agent, which Claude handles directly through its own Gmail, Calendar and Drive/Sheets connectors in a normal chat.

It is a Telegram bot that people message and expect immediate replies from, so it needs an always-on webhook server to receive Telegram updates and respond, which Claude scheduled tasks, skills or artifacts cannot provide.

Only the owner sends TikTok links to the Telegram bot, so a Claude skill can take the link in chat and make the same calls with the owner's API keys (RapidAPI, Cloudinary, OpenAI, Perplexity, Captions.ai, JSON2Video, Blotato) plus Google Sheets, with the short render waits handled in the same run and no public server needed.

It is a manually triggered set of OpenAI demo calls (chat, completions, DALL-E images, and an optional, disabled Whisper transcription) that can be run as a skill or an artifact with a Run button, calling the OpenAI HTTP API with the owner's API key or using Claude models instead.

This is a private chat agent with web search and short-term memory: the chat trigger isn't made public, so only the owner uses it, and Claude can do the same thing directly as a skill the owner chats with, using its own web search or a SerpAPI call with the owner's key.

The chat trigger isn't set to public, so this is the owner chatting with a web-searching agent, which works as a Claude skill using Claude's own web search (or SerpAPI with the owner's key) and Wikipedia lookups, with conversation memory built in.

This is a simple chatbot (a chat trigger feeding a prompted LLM chain, and the chat isn't set to public), so the owner can recreate it as a Claude skill they chat with, either using Claude's own model or calling the Hugging Face inference API with their key.

This is a chat agent the owner talks to, which fetches webpages over plain HTTP and converts them to Markdown, so it can run as a Claude skill using Claude's own model and web fetching, with no public endpoint or n8n-only node needed.

The chat trigger isn't set to public, so this is the owner chatting with an AI agent that runs SQL on Postgres, which can become a Claude skill using a database connector or the database's HTTP API (for example Neon or Supabase) with the owner's credentials, with Claude replacing the OpenAI model and the memory.

A cloud scheduled task every 6 hours can use Claude to generate a stoic-themed tweet, retry until it fits 280 characters, and post it through the X API with the owner's API keys, with no server needed.

It polls a Google Sheet for new rows, scores each lead with an LLM, and writes the rating back, so it can run as a scheduled task (Desktop for every-minute polling, or cloud hourly) using the Google Drive/Sheets connector or API and a Claude model in place of GPT-4.

It is a manually started, one-off prompt that turns a fixed ideal customer profile into a list of seed keywords with a Claude model, which fits a skill or an artifact page with a Run button, and the results can be saved to Google Drive/Sheets or Notion through a connector.

A manually triggered run that fetches a page through Jina's HTTP API with an API key, extracts book data with a Claude model, and appends rows to Google Sheets can be a skill or an artifact Run button using HTTP and the Google Drive/Sheets connector.

It is a manually started batch job that fetches Google Maps search pages and business websites over plain HTTP, pulls emails out with regex and appends them to a Google Sheet, all of which a skill or artifact with a Run button can do using HTTP requests and the Google Drive/Sheets connector.

It is a manually run batch job (the 15-minute schedule is disabled) that reads zip codes and categories from Google Sheets, calls the Google Places API with the owner's key, and writes the results back to Sheets, so it can run as a Claude skill or a scheduled task using the Google Drive connector or the Sheets API plus HTTP calls.

A weekly schedule that reads a Google Sheet, calls the SSL-Checker.io HTTP API, updates the sheet and emails alerts via Gmail fits a Claude cloud scheduled task using the Google Drive/Gmail connectors and an HTTP call.

The workflow polls a Google Drive folder for new PDFs or images, has a model extract transactions into a categorized CSV, and uploads the result to Drive; a scheduled task using the Google Drive connector and Claude's own document and vision abilities can do all of this, with no one waiting on a reply.

This is a personal chat assistant that reads and creates the owner's Google Calendar events, so it can run as a skill the owner chats with in Claude using the Google Calendar connector, with no public chat page needed.

This is a simple chat assistant that answers the owner's prompts with a JSON prompt/response wrapper; the chat trigger isn't set to public, so it can become a Claude skill the owner chats with, using a Claude model instead of local Ollama (the data would no longer stay on the owner's machine).

This is a manually or schedule-triggered batch job that reads ideas from Google Sheets, generates an article and title with an LLM, creates an image through the OpenAI API, posts it to WordPress over its REST API, and updates the sheet, all of which a scheduled task or skill can do with connectors, API keys and Claude models.

A manually triggered workflow that sends a prompt to the Perplexity API with the owner's API key and tidies the answer can run as a skill or an artifact page with a Run button that makes the HTTP call.

A manually started batch job that calls the Ghost Genius HTTP API with the owner's key, scores companies with an AI model (Claude can stand in for GPT-4.1), and checks and appends rows in Google Sheets, so it fits as a skill or an artifact page with a Run button and has no webhook or special trigger.

It is a daily scheduled job that makes AI calls, calls HTTP APIs (fal.ai Veo3, Blotato) with API keys, reads and writes Google Sheets, and waits 5 minutes, all of which a Claude cloud scheduled task can do, and nothing needs to answer outside callers.
